title: The H<SUB>2</SUB> angular momentum ─ mass relation of local disc galaxies
question: Is there a relation between the specific angular momentum and the mass of molecular gas in local disc galaxies, what are its slope, intercept and scatter, and do analytic stability models or the SHARK semi-analytic model reproduce it?

data.angular_resolution: CO(2-1) maps at ~1 arcsec resolution; rotation curves at 150 pc

what.value: CO tilted-ring rotation curves (150 pc resolution) for the PHANGS-ALMA galaxies

evidence.quote: We used the rotation curves derived by (cite: lang_phangs_2020) for the PHANGS-ALMA sample, obtained using the commonly employed tilted-ring model of the observed velocity field

what.value: Molecular gas surface density profiles (and the four alpha_CO prescriptions) for 66 of the 70 galaxies

evidence.quote: We used the molecular gas surface density profiles provided by (cite: sun_molecular_2022) for 66 of our 70 galaxies.
provides four alternative prescriptions for the PHANGS-ALMA sample

what.value: Hubble types, distances, stellar masses, effective radii and SFRs of the galaxies

evidence.quote: In both tables, Hubble types, distances, and stellar masses are from (cite: leroy_surveyphangs-alma_2021).
We obtained the values for Hubble type, $R_{\rm e}$, SFR, and $M_{\ast}$ from (cite: leroy_surveyphangs-alma_2021).

what.value: H I rotation curves (tilted-ring) for NGC 2903, NGC 3351, NGC 3521, NGC 3627, NGC 1365, NGC 3621, NGC 4535, NGC 4536

evidence.quote: with H i rotation velocities (also from tilted-ring models) from (cite: di_teodoro_radial_2021) and (cite: ponomareva_detailed_2016).

what.value: H I rotation curves for NGC 253, NGC 300 and NGC 7793

evidence.quote: We obtained the H i rotation curves for NGC 253 from (cite: mancera_pina_impact_2022), NGC 300 from (cite: mancera_pina_baryonic_2021), and NGC 7793 from (cite: bacchini_volumetric_2019).

what.value: CO(2-1) to CO(1-0) line ratio R21 = 0.65

evidence.quote: where $R_{21} = 0.65$ is the adopted CO(2-1) to CO(1-0) line ratio (cite: den_brok_new_2021; leroy_low-j_2022)

what.value: Literature j_H2 and M_H2 values for 16 THINGS galaxies used for comparison

evidence.quote: In Fig. [2](#Fig_rela) we compare our results to the study of (cite: obreschkow_fundamental_2014), who analysed 16 nearby spiral galaxies from the THINGS survey (cite: walter_things_2008).
where we adopt an uncertainty of 0.1 dex (cite: leroy_surveyphangs-alma_2021)

recipe.method: Use PHANGS-ALMA CO tilted-ring rotation curves; supplement with literature H I rotation curves for eight galaxies, and use H I only for three galaxies; correct to the PHANGS distance and inclination

recipe.goal: Derive H2 surface density profiles with a master alpha_CO
recipe.method: Convert CO(2-1) intensity profiles to Sigma_H2 using R21 and alpha_CO(1-0); average four alpha_CO prescriptions (S20, MW, N12, B13) into a master alpha_CO, with the standard deviation as uncertainty and standard error propagation
key_parameters: alpha_CO,MW = 4.35 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1 for the Galactic-average prescription
assumptions: Combining the four calibrations is treated as a conservative way of capturing realistic uncertainties

recipe.goal: Fit rotation curves with analytic functions for extrapolation
recipe.method: Fit an arctan function first; use the multi-parameter function for five galaxies (NGC 300, NGC 1365, NGC 2903, NGC 3521, NGC 3627) with complex kinematics
Fit a polyexponential profile (Sigma_0, R_Sigma, c1, c2, c3); fit a sum of two polyexponential profiles when one is not flexible enough
assumptions: Gas surface densities decay exponentially at large radii

recipe.goal: Compute j_H2 and M_H2 by Monte Carlo and apply the convergence cut
recipe.method: Compute j(<R) = J/M by integrating R'^2 Sigma V and R' Sigma over radius up to 50 kpc for 100000 random MCMC realisations of the rotation-curve and surface-density parameters; take medians and 1 sigma as values and uncertainties; M_H2 from integrating the denominator; exclude galaxies with convergence factor R < 0.7
key_parameters: Convergence threshold R_min = 0.7; integration limit 50 kpc; 100000 realisations
assumptions: Flat rotation curves and exponentially decaying Sigma beyond the data, so extrapolation captures all of j

recipe.goal: Fit the j_H2-M_H2 power law and look for secondary dependences
recipe.method: Fit log j = alpha [log M_H2 - 9] + beta with orthogonal intrinsic scatter; analyse residuals against Hubble type, R_e, SFR, M_* and M_H2/M_*

recipe.goal: Compare with previous observations and with models
recipe.method: Compare with Obreschkow & Glazebrook (2014) for five overlapping galaxies; test the Romeo (2020) disc-stability scaling; compare with SHARK v2.0 disc galaxies
assumptions: H2 velocity dispersion scaling gamma ~ 0.05-0.2 taken from kinematic measurements in the literature

answer_key.quantity: Slope alpha of the log j_H2 - log M_H2 relation

evidence.quote: We find the best-fitting parameters to be $\alpha = 0.53 \pm 0.04$, $\beta = 2.62 \pm 0.02$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\perp}=0.11 \pm 0.02$.

answer_key.quantity: Intercept beta of the j_H2-M_H2 relation (log j in kpc km/s at log M_H2 = 9)

evidence.quote: We find the best-fitting parameters to be $\alpha = 0.53 \pm 0.04$, $\beta = 2.62 \pm 0.02$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\perp}=0.11 \pm 0.02$.

answer_key.quantity: Orthogonal intrinsic scatter of the j_H2-M_H2 relation

evidence.quote: We find the best-fitting parameters to be $\alpha = 0.53 \pm 0.04$, $\beta = 2.62 \pm 0.02$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\perp}=0.11 \pm 0.02$.

answer_key.quantity: Number of galaxies with converged j_H2 profiles (R >= 0.7)

evidence.quote: Applying the convergence cutoff results in a final sample of 51 galaxies with converged $j_{\rm H_2}$ profiles.
The best-fitting parameters are $\alpha = 0.66 \pm 0.08$, $\beta = 2.48 \pm 0.03$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\perp}=0.16 \pm 0.02$.

answer_key.quantity: Intercept of the j_H2-M_* relation (log j at log M_* = 10)

evidence.quote: The best-fitting parameters are $\alpha = 0.66 \pm 0.08$, $\beta = 2.48 \pm 0.03$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\perp}=0.16 \pm 0.02$.

answer_key.quantity: Orthogonal intrinsic scatter of the j_H2-M_* relation

evidence.quote: The best-fitting parameters are $\alpha = 0.66 \pm 0.08$, $\beta = 2.48 \pm 0.03$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\perp}=0.16 \pm 0.02$.

answer_key.quantity: p-value of the anti-correlation between j_H2 residuals and M_H2/M_*

evidence.quote: the only significant trend ($p-$value=0.003) observed in our residual analysis is a moderate anti-correlation between $\Delta_{j_{\rm H_2}-M_{\rm H_2}}$ and $M_{\rm H_2}/M_\ast$.

answer_key.quantity: Mean (median) difference in j_H2 versus Obreschkow & Glazebrook (2014) for 5 overlapping galaxies

evidence.quote: the mean (median) difference in $j_{\rm H_2}$ is 0.04 (0.13) dex, with a maximum discrepancy of approximately 0.25 dex

answer_key.quantity: Mean (median) difference in M_H2 versus Obreschkow & Glazebrook (2014), excluding NGC 7793

evidence.quote: The mean (median) difference, without taking NGC 7793 into account, is 0.32 (0.28) dex, with a maximum difference of about 0.7 dex.

answer_key.quantity: Median difference between integrated M_H2 and PHANGS-ALMA CO luminosities

evidence.quote: We find great agreement when comparing our values to the CO luminosities reported in (cite: leroy_surveyphangs-alma_2021), with a median difference of 0.03 dex.

answer_key.quantity: p-value of correlation between j_H2 and log R_e,H2 (j_H2-M_* plane)

evidence.quote: we find a robust positive correlation between $j_{\rm H_2}$ and $\log(R_{\rm e, H_2})$ with a $p$-value of $2 \times 10^{-9}$.

not_stated_but_needed: Priors ranges / bounds for the flat priors on the rotation-curve and surface-density parameters, and the emcee setup (walkers, steps, burn-in, convergence test)
Radial extent and handling of the Lang et al. (2020) rotation curve points (radii cut, error treatment) and the exact files/versions of the Lang et al. (2020) and Sun et al. (2022) products
Which galaxies needed a sum of two polyexponential profiles, and the criterion for choosing one versus two
Likelihood, sampler, priors and handling of x/y uncertainties for the Bayesian power-law fit with orthogonal intrinsic scatter, and how distance uncertainty enters
How the H I rotation curve velocities were joined to the CO curves (radius of transition, weighting)
Details of how the metallicity Z', mean CO intensity and total surface density needed for the alpha_CO prescriptions were taken from Sun et al. (2022)
Selection details of the SHARK sample (catalogue version, mass cuts, how j_H2 is defined in SHARK)
missing_for_reproduction: Priors, walker settings and convergence tests for the emcee fits
Likelihood and sampler for the Bayesian power-law fit with orthogonal intrinsic scatter
Numerical H I rotation-curve data and how they were merged with CO curves
Per-galaxy choice of function (one vs two polyexponentials)
No released analysis code or catalogue file named beyond Tables 1 and 2
score_reason: Public PHANGS products, explicit equations, sample cuts and numeric results (Tables 1-4), but fitting priors/likelihood and some per-galaxy choices are missing and no code is released
rediscovery_reason: Inputs are public PHANGS-ALMA derived products, the pipeline is a short set of integrals and fits with numeric targets (alpha 0.53, beta 2.62, 51 galaxies), though priors and H I curve details must be assumed
